dialogue.content: おはようございます。本日はよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. Thank you for your time today. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: おはようございます。こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: お返事ありがとうございます。お時間になりましたら、改めて始めさせていただきますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your reply. We will begin properly at the scheduled time.

dialogue.content: お返事ありがとうございます。お時間になりましたら、改めて始めさせていただきますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your reply. We will begin properly at the scheduled time.

dialogue.content: こんにちは、本日はご相談ありがとうございます。まず、性別、年齢、ご相談内容を教えてください。
dialogue.English: Hello, thank you for coming in for a consultation today. First, could you please tell me your gender, age, and what you would like to discuss?

dialogue.content: こんにちは。女性、30歳、夫婦関係
dialogue.English: Hello. Female, 30 years old, marital relationship issues.

dialogue.content: 教えてくださってありがとうございます。夫婦関係でどんなことがありましたか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. What has been happening in your marriage?

dialogue.content: 旦那が嫌で、仕事から帰って来たり、休みの日になると気持ちが落ち着きません
dialogue.English: I can't stand my husband, and when he comes home from work or on his days off, I feel on edge.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。夫さんと一緒にいるのが嫌ということでしょうか。嫌というのはどんな感じですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is it that you dislike being with your husband? What does that dislike feel like for you?

dialogue.content: たとえば、生理的に無理だとか、イライラするとかですね。
dialogue.English: For example, does it feel physically repulsive, or do you feel irritated?

dialogue.content: そんな感じです！落ち着かなくて、ざわざわします
dialogue.English: That's it! I feel restless and agitated.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。家に夫さんがいるとざわざわして落ち着かないと、相談者さんも気持ちが休まりませんよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. If you feel agitated and unsettled when your husband is home, you must not be able to relax at all.

dialogue.content: いつごろから夫さんを嫌だなと感じましたか？
dialogue.English: Around when did you start feeling this dislike toward your husband?

dialogue.content: そうです。子どもたちと3人だと楽しく過ごせるのですが、夫がいると気配を消したくなるというか、、、なんか嫌です
dialogue.English: That's right. When it's just the three of us, my children and I, we have a good time, but when my husband is around, I feel like I want to make myself invisible... I just don't like it.

dialogue.content: 前から思っていたのですが、年明けから強く思うようになりました
dialogue.English: I've felt this way for a while, but it's become much stronger since the beginning of the year.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね…。夫さんと二人きりだと、緊張感があったり、夫さんに意識されたくない感覚になるのですね。
dialogue.English: I see... So when you're alone with your husband, you feel tense, and you have this sense of not wanting to be noticed by him.

dialogue.content: なるほど、前からあったけれども年明けからさらに強くなったんですね。年明けごろにはどんなことがありましたか？
dialogue.English: I see, so it's been there for a while but intensified after the New Year. Did anything happen around that time?

dialogue.content: 2人きりの空間はなるべく作らないようにしています、子ども達が一緒でも夫がいると嫌です
dialogue.English: I try to avoid being alone with him as much as possible. Even when the children are with us, I still don't like it when he's there.

dialogue.content: 年明けに私たち家族に向けてではないのですが、知人に対して暴力的な部分を見てそこからです
dialogue.English: At the start of the year, it wasn't directed at our family, but I saw a violent side of him toward an acquaintance, and that's when it started.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。お子さんがいても、夫さんがいると相談者様は嫌な気持ちになってしまうのですね。それは安らげず、お辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. So even with your children present, you feel uncomfortable when your husband is there. It must be hard not being able to feel at peace.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そんなことがあったのですね…。それはショックでしたよね。夫さんは知人の方に対してどんなことをしたのですか？
dialogue.English: So that's what happened... That must have been a shock. What did your husband do to this acquaintance?

dialogue.content: ショックというより怖いです蹴る、倒れているのに顔を踏む
dialogue.English: More than shocking, it was scary. He kicked him, and even when he was down, he stomped on his face.

dialogue.content: 夫さんが知人の方に蹴ったり踏んだり、物理的に暴力をふるったのですね…！それは夫さんを怖くなってしまっても仕方ないですね。それを見たとき、ご相談者様はどうしていましたか？
dialogue.English: Your husband physically assaulted the acquaintance, kicking and stomping on him... It's completely understandable that you would become afraid of him. What were you doing when you saw this?

dialogue.content: ただ怖くて、口ではやめてって言ってたけど知人が一瞬意識を無くしてしまってそうなる前になんで止められなかったんだろうって後悔と恐怖です
dialogue.English: I was just so scared. I verbally told him to stop, but the acquaintance lost consciousness for a moment, and I'm filled with regret and fear, wondering why I couldn't stop it before it got to that point.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。ご相談者様も怖くて仕方なかったと思いますが、「やめて」と止めようとしたんですね。力の差がある中、それでも止めようとしたご相談者様の優しい気持ちや正義感が伝わってきます。そうなる前に止めたかったと後悔もあったんですね。意識を失うほどの暴力、恐怖して当然です。知人の方は何をして夫さんを怒らせてしまったのでしょう？
dialogue.English: I see. I imagine you must have been terrified, but you still tried to stop him by saying 'stop.' Despite the difference in strength, your kindness and sense of justice in trying to intervene really come through. You also felt regret for not being able to stop it sooner. It's only natural to be horrified by violence that causes someone to lose consciousness. What did the acquaintance do to make your husband so angry?

dialogue.content: 後輩が3人家にきていたのですが、お酒も飲んでいて悪ふざけが過ぎた感じです。お酒の席とはいえ悪ふざけが過ぎた後輩達も悪いですが、夫はそこまでやる事なのかと理解出来ません
dialogue.English: Three junior colleagues had come over to our home, and they were drinking and their horseplay went too far. Even though it was a drinking situation and the juniors were at fault for taking it too far, I can't understand why my husband had to go that far.

dialogue.content: なるほど…。お酒の席でのことだったんですね。相手が悪ふざけをしていたとしても、意識を失うほどの暴力はいき過ぎですよね…。夫さんを理解できないと感じたんですね。家族として、悲しい気持ちもきっとありますよね。
dialogue.English: I see... So it happened while they were drinking. Even if the other person was joking around too much, violence that causes someone to lose consciousness is going too far... You felt that you couldn't understand your husband. As his family, you must also feel a sense of sadness.

dialogue.content: 悲しいという気持ちもありますが怖いが一番です
dialogue.English: I do feel sad, but fear is the strongest feeling.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。とにかく怖いというお気持ちなんですね。この件についてどなたかに度相談しましたか？
dialogue.English: I see. So the main feeling is simply fear. Have you spoken to anyone about this incident?

dialogue.content: 姉に相談しました
dialogue.English: I talked to my older sister.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。お姉さまはどんな反応でしたか？
dialogue.English: I see. How did your sister react?

dialogue.content: (誤字失礼いたしました。)
dialogue.English: (My apologies for the typo.)

dialogue.content: そんなところを目の前で見たら怖くなって当然だよといった感じです
dialogue.English: She said something like, 'It's only natural to feel scared after seeing something like that happen right in front of you.'

dialogue.content: ご相談者様は、お姉さまの反応を見て、どう感じましたか？
dialogue.English: How did you feel hearing your sister's reaction?

dialogue.content: やっぱりそうなんだ、理解してくれると思いました
dialogue.English: I thought, 'So it isn't just me,' and I felt that she understood.

dialogue.content: お姉さまの反応を見て、わかってくれたと安心したのですね。ほっとしましたよね。
dialogue.English: Hearing her response, you felt understood and reassured. It was a relief, wasn't it?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ご相談者様は、今後、夫婦関係がどうなったら良いなと思いますか？
dialogue.English: What do you hope for in your marital relationship going forward?

dialogue.content: 結婚生活がずっと続くとは思えません。子どもが高校か大学生卒業するまでは続けばいいなと思いますが、先が長いので不安です
dialogue.English: I don't think this marriage can last forever. I hope we can stay together until our children graduate from high school or university, but that's a long way off, and I'm anxious.

dialogue.content: なるほど。結婚生活が長く続くとは感じていないのですね。でも、お子さんの成長のことを考えると父親はいたほうが良いという考えをお持ちなんですね。ご相談者様自身には、夫さんはどのように接していますか？
dialogue.English: I see. So you don't feel the marriage will last long-term. But you also feel that it's better for the children to have their father around while they're growing up. How does your husband treat you personally?

dialogue.content: そうです。必要最低限の会話のみという感じです。休みの日はほぼ夫は寝ているので一緒に出かける事もないです
dialogue.English: That's right. We only have the bare minimum of conversation. On his days off, he mostly just sleeps, so we never go out together.

dialogue.content: お子さんのためには父親がいたほうが良いけど、普段お二人の間では必要最低限の会話だけで、今後、家庭が保てるかと考えたらとても不安ですよね。
dialogue.English: So you think it's better for the children to have their father, but with only minimal conversation between you two, it must be very worrying to think about whether you can maintain the household in the future.

dialogue.content: そうなんです
dialogue.English: Exactly.

dialogue.content: ただこんな夫婦を見ている子どもが幸せなのかも分からないです
dialogue.English: But I also don't know if our children can be happy seeing their parents like this.

dialogue.content: なるほど。お子さんがこの家庭の雰囲気を感じて幸せに思うか、も不安なんですね。ご相談者様のお子様思いの気持ちが伝わってきました。
dialogue.English: I see. You're also worried about whether your children can feel happy, sensing the atmosphere at home. Your deep care for your children really comes through.

dialogue.content: 子どもには幸せになって欲しいし、家庭が安心出来る場所であって欲しいけどその環境を作ってあげられているか不安です
dialogue.English: I want my children to be happy, and I want our home to be a safe and secure place for them, but I'm worried about whether I'm able to create that environment.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。お子さんには幸せになって欲しい、それをサポートしたいという強いお気持ちがあるのですね。そうしたお気持ちが強いほど、不安も出てきますよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. You have a strong desire for your children to be happy and to support them. The stronger those feelings are, the more anxiety can arise.

dialogue.content: お子さんは、年明けの事件以降どんな様子ですか？
dialogue.English: How have your children been since the incident at the start of the year?

dialogue.content: 子ども達は寝ていたのでその場面を見ていませんし、言ってもいないので何も知りません
dialogue.English: The children were asleep, so they didn't see it. I haven't told them either, so they don't know anything about it.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。その場面に居合わせなかったのは良かったですね。その後、ご相談者様の夫さんへの嫌な気持ちは大きくなったと聞きましたが、そういった雰囲気を感じている様子はなさそうですか？
dialogue.English: I see. It's good that they weren't present for that. You mentioned that your negative feelings toward your husband have grown since then; do they seem to have picked up on that atmosphere?

dialogue.content: 感じていると思います。なので会話も必要最低限だし、寝ていて出かけるのも一緒に行かないんだと思います。
dialogue.English: I think they do sense it. That's why conversations are minimal, and when he's sleeping, we go out without him.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね…。であれば、お子さんもなんとなく夫さんとご相談者様の雰囲気をわかっているかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: I see... In that case, your children might be vaguely aware of the atmosphere between you and your husband.

dialogue.content: やはりそうですよね、
dialogue.English: I figured as much.

dialogue.content: ご相談者様の落ち着かない気持ちや、お子さんへの不安を感じる機会を減らすにはどんなことができそうでしょうか？たとえば、親御さんやお姉さんのところにお子さんとしばらくいてみるとか、ご相談者様とお子さんだけで少し遠出をしてみるとかですね。
dialogue.English: What might be possible to reduce the times you feel unsettled and anxious about the children? For example, staying with your parents or your sister for a while with the kids, or taking a short trip with just you and the children.

dialogue.content: 実家と姉の所は遠いので気軽に預けられません。近場の買い物だといいのですが、遠出をして私たちだけ楽しむとあまりいい顔をしないので、、
dialogue.English: My parents' and sister's homes are far away, so I can't easily arrange for the children to stay there. A short shopping trip nearby is fine, but if we go on a longer trip and have fun without him, he doesn't react well...

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。夫さんも置いていかれるのは嫌といった様子なのですね。ご相談者様は離れたいのに、困ってしまいますね。
dialogue.English: I see. So your husband seems displeased about being left behind. That must be troubling for you, since you want some distance.

dialogue.content: そうですね、でも子どもは望んでいないかもしれないので私のわがままに振り回すのも可哀想で
dialogue.English: That's right... but the children might not want that, and I feel it would be unfair to drag them along with my selfish wishes.

dialogue.content: お子さんは父親として夫さんを好いている様子なのですね？お子さんのことを一番に考えてらっしゃるんですね。本当にお子さん思いですね。
dialogue.English: So it seems your children like your husband as their father? You're really putting your children first. You are truly devoted to them.

dialogue.content: 好きかは分かりませんが、嫌いではないと思います
dialogue.English: I'm not sure if they like him, but I don't think they dislike him.

dialogue.content: 嫌いではなさそうなんですね…。ますます悩ましいですね。本日はお時間になってしまいました。まだ不安なことも残っていると思いますので、記録を残して次回続きからお話を聞けるようにしておきます。
dialogue.English: So they don't seem to dislike him... That makes it even more complicated. Our time is up for today. I'm sure you still have anxieties, so I will keep a record of our conversation so we can pick up where we left off next time.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 今日のお話を聞いてご相談者様は、夫さんの他の人への態度で怖いと感じてしまったとのことでした。ご相談者様は優しく正義感もありとてもお子様思いの方です。今後、お子さんとご相談者様の安心と幸せへの道が必ず見つかると思います。
dialogue.English: From our conversation today, I understand that you've come to feel fear because of your husband's behavior towards others. You are a kind person with a strong sense of justice and you care deeply for your children. I believe that you will surely find a path to safety and happiness for you and your children in the future.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 本日は貴重なお時間ありがとうございました。大事なことなので、慎重に考えていきましょう。(お時間ありがとうございました。終了してよろしいですか？)
dialogue.English: Thank you for your valuable time today. This is an important matter, so let's think about it carefully together. (Thank you for your time. Is it okay to end the session?)

dialogue.content: （大丈夫です）
dialogue.English: (That's fine.)
